findings.title: Client-settable x-vercel-isr header re-enables x_astro_path path override (CWE-290, A01 Broken Access Control)
findings.why_it_matters: The fix trusts a plain request header (`x-vercel-isr: 1`) as proof that the request came from Vercel's ISR rewrite, then lets the `x_astro_path` query param rewrite the URL pathname with no secret. If the Vercel edge does not strip or overwrite that header on external requests, any client can send `x-vercel-isr: 1` plus `?x_astro_path=/protected` to a function that is reachable without the edge middleware and get the protected route rendered. That is the exact bypass that #15959 closed (the secret check existed so the override could not be forged). I confirmed in-process against the built fixture that the header alone flips the behaviour: without it `/api/public?x_astro_path=/api/private` returns id=public, with it the response is id=private. Whether the header is forgeable on the platform could not be verified offline.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not use a client-settable header as the trust signal. Assumption: Vercel cannot inject the middleware secret into the ISR rewrite, so scope the override instead: (1) add a build-time flag to the virtual:astro-vercel:config module that is true only for the _isr function bundle and honour the query param only when it is set, so _render never accepts it; and (2) after computing the new URL, require app.match(newRequest) to resolve to a non-excluded ISR route, otherwise ignore the override. If Vercel documents that x-vercel-isr is overwritten at the edge, cite that in a code comment and keep the header check as the secondary guard.
evidence: packages/integrations/vercel/src/index.ts:490 -- : ISR_PATH; ISR-routed pages skip MIDDLEWARE_PATH, so the override on _isr/_render is the only thing standing between the URL and the route that renders
provenance: 335a20416 Matthew Phillips 2026-03-19 - Require trusted secret for path overrides (#15959)

residual_risks: Could not verify offline whether Vercel strips or overwrites an inbound x-vercel-isr header, or sets it on direct requests to /_isr; the finding's exploitability depends on this.
The same entrypoint serves both _render and _isr, so any function reachable directly at /_render or /_isr accepts the ISR override once the header is present.
testing_gaps: test/path-override-security.test.js has no case sending `x-vercel-isr: 1` with `x_astro_path` on the _render function to assert the override is rejected, and no positive ISR case asserting the legitimate override still works. Both would pin the trust boundary this change moves.
